question: Does a per-chat permission grant survive a project switch, and does this change widen that to the viewer- and quota-effect tools?
howRecorded: Each review run carried the claim as a finding and then put it to two independent verifiers with distinct lenses (verify:correctness:* and verify:reproduce:*), each instructed to try to refute it. Copied verbatim from the runs' journals; the journals themselves live in the session directory, not in this repo.

claims.label: review:gate
claims.claim: The "Allow for this chat" registry is one module-global Set that chat-level resets only clear for the project they are invoked on, so a grant made in one project's chat authorises the same gated tool silently in every other project's chat.
claims.failureScenario: Ask mode. In project A the assistant calls generate_render_visualisation and the user clicks "Allow for this chat" (permissions.ts:151 adds the tool name to the shared grantedForChat Set). The user then switches to project B: switchProject (studio/assistant/projectSwitch.ts) touches no permission state, and the only resetChatGrants callers are the current jobId's chat actions (useAssistantChat.ts:299, 301, 312, 317), so the grant survives the switch. In project B's chat — a different archived thread, since useChats records and readChatArchive are keyed by jobId — the assistant calls the same tool and permissionVerdict returns "allowed" at permissions.ts:33, so no prompt is shown in a chat where the user was never asked, and the render runs (spending the metered render quota the class was gated for). navigate_workspace behaves identically: an "allow for this chat" given while reading one project lets the assistant move the workspace unprompted in the next project. The documented scope is the chat: "for this chat grants live until the chat is cleared or continued" (permissions.ts:9-10).

claims.label: review:gate
claims.claim: "Allow for this chat" records the tool name in one process-global Set that no project switch clears, so in ask mode a grant given in one project's chat silently authorises the same tool in a different project's chat — an exposure this diff widens from project edits to navigation, viewer changes, the drafting animation and a metered render, because permissionVerdict (the line the diff changed) now consults grantedForChat for all five effectful tools.
claims.failureScenario: Ask mode. In project A the user clicks "Allow for this chat" on navigate_workspace (or save_project / draw_architect_elements / generate_render_visualisation); decide() at permissions.ts:151 adds the name to the single module-scope grantedForChat Set, and the only callers of resetChatGrants() are chat-level actions inside one project (useAssistantChat.ts:299, 301, 312, 317). The user then switches project via LiveAssistant.tsx:567 openProject -> projectSwitch.switchProject, which contains no permission or grant handling (grep for permission/grant/reset/clear in projectSwitch.ts is empty), and the hook's project-change path only runs ensureChat(jobId), not activateChat. In project B — whose chat archive is a different stored conversation (useChats.records[jobId], readChatArchive(jobId)) that the user never granted anything in — the assistant calls the same tool name, gateToolCall -> permissionVerdict(name, "ask", grantedForChat) returns "allowed" at line 33, so the prompt is skipped and the action runs. The user is never asked in the conversation where the action happens, which contradicts the feature's own doc comment ("'for this chat' grants live until the chat is cleared or continued"). The suite cannot catch it: permissions.test.ts only grants and re-calls within one store instance and has no notion of project or chat identity.

verdicts.label: verify:correctness:gate
verdicts.reasoning: The claim is substantiated by the source. permissions.ts:124 creates a module-global zustand store (no jobId keying, no browserSingleton wrapper like the chat runtime uses), and grantedForChat is one shared Set<string> (permissions.ts:126). decide("chat") mutates that single Set (permissions.ts:151). resetChatGrants (permissions.ts:154) is invoked only from the current jobId's chat actions in useAssistantChat.ts:299/301/312/317; nothing invokes it on a project switch. switchProject (projectSwitch.ts:77) contains no permission handling and performs an in-place retryProjectLoad() rather than a page reload, and the [jobId, hydrated] effect (LiveAssistant.tsx:230-240) resets only draft/attachments/messages/references. Chat archives are per-project (readChatArchive(projectId), chatHistory.ts:57), so project B's chat is a different thread that inherits the grant. permissionVerdict (permissions.ts:33) therefore returns "allowed" for the granted effectful tool in project B without a prompt, and the tool runs (the render spends quota), contradicting the documented scope in permissions.ts:9-10 ("for this chat grants live until the chat is cleared or continued"). The change is what makes this newly reachable for navigate_workspace/generate_render_visualisation (they were previously ungated in VIEW_TOOLS). The claim's one imprecision — that resets "only clear for the project they are invoked on" — is not a refutation: resetChatGrants clears globally, but is only ever invoked for the current project's chat actions, so the net effect (grant survives the switch) is exactly as claimed. None of the accepted verification exercises switch-plus-grant (all three live runs are single-project), so this is a hole the tests miss.

verdicts.label: verify:reproduce:gate
verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this: the described state is reachable, and every factual assertion in the claim checks out against the source.

Reachability chain, verified by reading the files:
1. `usePermissions` is one module-level zustand store (permissions.ts:124-126) and `grantedForChat` is a single `Set<string>` with no jobId/chat key. A "chat" decision writes only the tool name into it (permissions.ts:151), and `permissionVerdict` short-circuits to "allowed" whenever that Set contains the tool (permissions.ts:33). So the grant is per-tool, not per-project.
2. `resetChatGrants()` has exactly four callers — useAssistantChat.ts:299 (restoreHistory), :301 (continueInNewChat), :312 (archiveHistory), :317 (clear) — all invoked from the currently-open jobId's chat actions. Nothing resets grants when the open project changes.
3. The switch is in-place: projectSwitch.ts:152 re-hydrates through `store.retryProjectLoad()` → `hydratePersistence()` with no `location.reload`, so the module singleton survives. useAssistantChat.ts:50-55 only aborts controllers on a job change, and LiveAssistant's jobId-keyed effects (230-240, 250-259) reset draft/UI/library state only. No permission state is touched.
4. The five effectful tools are in `VIEW_TOOLS` (skills.ts:101-113), so in ask mode they are declared to the model; `gateToolCall` (permissions.ts:158-166) reads the live global grant and returns null with no prompt.

Concrete failing case: ask mode, project A's chat, the model calls navigate_workspace and the user clicks "Allow for this chat" → grantedForChat = {navigate_workspace}. Switch to project B (a different archived thread, records keyed by jobId in useChats). In B's chat the model calls navigate_workspace again; permissionVerdict sees mode "ask" but grantedForChat.has(toolName) → "allowed", so gateToolCall returns null, no card is shown, and the workspace moves unprompted. generate_render_visualisation behaves identically and spends the quota the change gated it for. This matches the documented per-chat scope being violated (permissions.ts:9-10, "for this chat grants live until the chat is cleared or continued").

The claim's only imprecision is that `resetChatGrants` actually clears the whole Set globally (permissions.ts:154) rather than "only for the project they are invoked on" — but that does not weaken the conclusion, since no reset is invoked on a project switch, so the grant still leaks. None of the verified evidence (typecheck, the 1,717-test suite, or the three live runs — tools-prohibited delivery, readonly refusing navigate_workspace, ask-mode Deny) exercises a project switch with a standing grant, so this is exactly the kind of case those would miss. I could produce the specific inputs and state, so it is not refuted.

verdicts.label: verify:correctness:gate
verdicts.reasoning: The claim's mechanics all hold up against the source. `grantedForChat` is a plain module-scope Set on a bare zustand store (permissions.ts:124-126), keyed only by tool name (permissions.ts:151), and the sole reset — `resetChatGrants` (permissions.ts:154) — is invoked from exactly four chat-level actions inside one project (useAssistantChat.ts:299 restoreHistory, 301 continueInNewChat, 312 archiveHistory, 317 clear). A project switch does not touch it: LiveAssistant.openProject (LiveAssistant.tsx:567) calls switchProject (projectSwitch.ts:77), which re-hydrates the studio store via retryProjectLoad under a navigator.locks guard and contains no permission/grant/clear handling, and the jobId-change path only runs ensureChat (useAssistantChat.ts:133) plus beginGovernedWork — it never calls activateChat and never resets grants. After the switch, gateToolCall (permissions.ts:158-160) reads the surviving Set, so permissionVerdict returns "allowed" at the changed line 33 and the prompt is skipped in project B. The diff does extend that consultation to the five effectful tools: `isAssistantEditTool` -> `isAssistantGatedTool` (skills.ts:138) makes grantedForChat decisive for navigate_workspace/show_design_in_model/hide_designed_model/control_draftsman/generate_render_visualisation, and all five are in VIEW_TOOLS (skills.ts:101,104,111-113), hence declared in ask mode, so the project-B call is reachable. The suite cannot see it: permissions.test.ts only exercises a single store instance with no project/chat identity. One imprecision worth noting but not a refutation — pre-diff these effectful tools were ungated in every mode, so the cross-project leak for them is not strictly a *larger* total exposure (the diff adds the prompts); what the diff genuinely widens is the set of tools whose chat grants survive a project switch, and the described outcome (project-B prompt skipped because of a grant given in project A) does occur.

verdicts.label: verify:reproduce:gate
verdicts.reasoning: I could not refute this. The grant store is a single module-scope zustand Set, written only at permissions.ts:151 and read at permissions.ts:33; the diff changes permissions.ts:31 to isAssistantGatedTool, so the five EFFECTFUL_TOOLS now reach line 33 and are satisfied by any stored grant. Nothing clears it on a project switch: switchProject (projectSwitch.ts) contains no permission/grant handling, its only store calls are saveCurrentProject / setState({persistenceRecoveryBlocked}) / retryProjectLoad, and retryProjectLoad is an in-memory re-hydrate (store.ts:2216-2219), not a reload, so module state survives. The only resetChatGrants callers in the repo are the four chat-level actions (useAssistantChat.ts:299,301,312,317); the jobId-change path (useAssistantChat.ts:133) runs only ensureChat(jobId), and each project's conversation is a distinct readChatArchive(jobId)/useChats.records[jobId]. I executed the shipping module and reproduced the failure: ask mode, gateToolCall("navigate_workspace") prompted, decide(id,"chat") stored the grant, and a later call of the same tool returned null with pending===null (no prompt) because permissionVerdict(...,"ask",grantedForChat)==="allowed". The claim's line citations (permissions.ts:33,151; useAssistantChat.ts:299,301,312,317; LiveAssistant.tsx:567) are all exact. The only imprecision is "widens": pre-diff these five were ungated and ran silently in every project, so the diff makes silent execution conditional rather than adding it. But the per-chat grant is an artifact this diff newly routes the five tools through, and its leaking across conversations is a reachable semantic hole the suite cannot catch — the new permissions.test.ts:30 models the grant as a bare Set([name]) with no chat or project identity.
